dedupe_keys.name: topochange topology change synthetic data set for distribution state estimation

description: TopoChange is a data set for testing how state estimation methods cope with changes in power network topology. It was published on IEEE DataPort by Jialin He and Hajali Bayramov. It holds processed real household load profiles from a Spanish smart meter data set, additional synthetic profiles generated from them, and power flow results for different topologies: customers are assigned to load buses of the CIGRE medium-voltage benchmark network, the topology is changed by switching, and voltages are computed with the Power Grid Model for each load snapshot and topology. The authors used it to test a physics-informed neural network with synthetic training data. Coverage is the generic CIGRE network with Spanish-derived loads, so the method is location-independent. The files, about 306 MB, are downloadable from IEEE DataPort after login, under CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: the page states that file access needs a login and shows a subscription notice, and the network is a benchmark, not a real system. Simulation uses are robustness testing of state estimation and grid digital twins under switching. Related records: model-power-grid-model is the solver used.
